Exercise 8.1 · Week 8

Test the Clamp

Python in Thonny Work in pairs

Goal: write your first pytest tests, and learn to read PASSED and FAILED.

clamp(value, low, high) in clamp_tools.py keeps a number between two limits. Games use it to stop a player walking off the screen: clamp(99, 0, 10) gives 10.

  1. Install pytest once (ask your teacher): Tools > Manage packages..., type pytest, click Search, then Install. No account needed.
  2. Read clamp_tools.py. Do not change it: it is correct.
  3. Open starter.py. This is YOUR test file. Press Run. You will see one line per test, ending in PASSED or FAILED.
  4. TODO 1 and TODO 2: write an assert line in each empty test.
  5. TODO 3: write a fourth test for a value exactly on a limit.
  6. Try it: change one expected answer to something wrong and press Run. Read the FAILED message. Then change it back.

Done looks like:

starter.py::test_middle_value_stays_the_same PASSED
starter.py::test_too_small_goes_up_to_low PASSED
starter.py::test_too_big_comes_down_to_high PASSED
...

The programmer way: Tools > Open system shell..., then type python -m pytest starter.py -v and press Return. (If it says "command not found", type python3 instead of python.)

Starter code

Open starter.py in Thonny, or copy the code below into a new file and save it as starter.py.

"""MY TESTS for clamp()  -  this file is YOUR test file.

Press the green Run button: pytest runs every function whose name starts
with test_ and says PASSED or FAILED for each one.

A test calls the function with values YOU choose and checks the answer:
    assert clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5, "message to show if it is wrong"

Read clamp_tools.py first to see what clamp() should do.
"""

from clamp_tools import clamp


def test_middle_value_stays_the_same():
    # Normal case: 5 is already between 0 and 10.
    assert clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5, "5 is between 0 and 10, so it should stay 5"


def test_too_small_goes_up_to_low():
    # TODO 1: clamp(-3, 0, 10) should give 0.
    #         Write an assert line like the one in the first test.
    pass


def test_too_big_comes_down_to_high():
    # TODO 2: choose a value that is too big. What should clamp() give back?
    pass


# TODO 3 (edge case): write a 4th test for a value exactly ON a limit,
#                     like clamp(10, 0, 10). Its name must start with test_


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pytest
    pytest.main(["-v", __file__])
Download starter.py

Stuck? Open a hint

Try on your own first. Hints open one at a time, from a small nudge to a bigger one. None of them gives the answer away.

Hint 1: Where to look

Look at the first test in starter.py. It is finished, so copy its pattern. Then read the examples at the top of clamp_tools.py to work out the right answers for your own tests.

Hint 2: Try this

Each test needs an assert line. It calls clamp() with numbers you choose and checks the answer using ==. Work out the right answer by hand first. Then write it after the ==.

Hint 3: Almost there

Shape to fill in: assert clamp(____, 0, 10) == ____, "message". For a too-big value, pick a number above 10. For a value on a limit, use 0 or 10 as the first number. A new test needs a name that starts with test_.
